extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners who practice before the USPTO (particularly trademark/non-patent practitioners), counsel involved in USPTO disciplinary matters, and Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO disciplinary standards, regulatory provisions, and procedural requirements governing practitioner conduct before the Office (with emphasis on trademark/non-patent practice), and the rules/procedures for consent exclusion and reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) — Disreputable or gross misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in disreputable or gross misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the Order: directing or allowing employees to prepare, sign, and file trademark applications, responses to Office Actions, and other trademark documents without attorney involvement or supervision; directing or allowing employees to provide legal advice and guidance to trademark applicants; failing to comply with USPTO electronic signature rules by not personally electronically signing trademark applications and documents and instead directing or allowing employees to sign or forge his electronic signature; directing or allowing employees to sign or forge § 2(f) declarations; failing to adequately supervise employees permitting creation/fileing of false or fraudulent specimens or digitally altered images; failing to inform clients or the USPTO of potentially invalid registrations resulting from false filings; collecting fees while representations were not actually performed by an attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) — Dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: not informing clients that their documents were not prepared/reviewed by an attorney; not personally electronically signing documents and thereby misleading USPTO/clients/public; directing or allowing employees to sign or forge § 2(f) declarations when employees lacked requisite knowledge; permitting or filing false/fraudulent specimens or digitally altered images that jeopardize validity of trademarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) — Conduct prejudicial to administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: allowing employees to prepare/sign/file trademark applications and documents or provide legal advice without supervision; failing to review employee-prepared applications and responses before filing; failing to comply with electronic signature rules (leading to jeopardized registrations); permitting forged/unauthorized signatures or false § 2(f) declarations that mislead Examining Attorneys.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) — Conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in any other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all for conduct referenced elsewhere in counts (e.g., failing to supervise employees, permitting false specimens, forging signatures, failing to inform clients/USPTO).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(2)(ii) — Knowingly giving false or misleading information
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowingly giving false or misleading information or knowingly participating materially in giving false or misleading information to the USPTO or any USPTO employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: directing or allowing employees to sign or forge § 2(f) declarations and filing them when the practitioner knew Examining Attorneys would rely on them or when employees lacked adequate knowledge to aver distinctiveness; fostering filings that mislead the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(15) — Violating certifications under 37 C.F.R. § 11.18
rubrics_metrics.description: Violating the certifications made to the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include allowing employees to sign/forge the practitioner's electronic signature on documents or § 2(f) declarations when actual signatory not identified and/or lacked knowledge; failing to adequately supervise employees resulting in false/digitally altered specimens being filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.31(a) — Deceiving or misleading prospective applicants (advertising)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deceiving or misleading prospective applicants or other persons having business before the Office by word, circular, letter, or advertising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: advertising on a firm's website that trademark applications would be prepared by an attorney when in fact they were not prepared or reviewed by an attorney prior to filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.47(a) and (c) — Aiding unauthorized practice of law before the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Aiding a non-practitioner in the unauthorized practice of law before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: directing or allowing employees to prepare, sign, and file trademark applications and other trademark documents; allowing employees to provide legal advice or communicate with clients about trademark searches/opinions without attorney involvement; not reviewing employee-prepared trademark documents before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.48 — Sharing legal fees with a non-practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Sharing legal fees with a non-practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: paying employees non-discretionary monthly bonuses tied to proceeds generated by trademark legal services provided to applicants with whom they interacted (constitutes sharing legal fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(b) — Handling matters without adequate preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling a legal matter without preparation adequate under the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: failing to comply with electronic signature rules by not personally signing trademark applications and documents and allowing others to sign, jeopardizing validity of registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) — Neglecting client matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Neglecting client matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: not reviewing trademark applications, responses to Office Actions, and other documents prepared and filed by employees before filing; failing to adequately supervise employees leading to false/fraudulent specimens or digitally altered images being filed; failing to inform clients of potential invalidity and failing to take remedial action or offer restitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a)(1) — Failing to seek lawful objectives of a client
rubrics_metrics.description: Intentionally failing to seek the lawful objectives of a client through reasonably available means permitted by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: intentionally failing to inform clients that their registrations or applications were potentially invalid and failing to take timely and effective remedial action or offer restitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a)(3) — Intentionally prejudicing or damaging the client
rubrics_metrics.description: Intentionally prejudicing or damaging the client during the course of a professional relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: intentionally failing to inform clients of potential invalidity or failing to remedy or offer restitution, thereby harming the client.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.89(c)(6) — Intentionally or habitually violating Code provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Intentionally or habitually violating any provision of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility while appearing in a professional capacity before a tribunal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: directing employees to prepare/sign/file documents or provide legal advice without supervision; failing to comply with electronic signature rules; allowing false/digital specimens to be filed; failing to inform USPTO of potentially invalid filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.112(a) — Failing to deposit advance legal fees into client trust account
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to deposit legal fees paid in advance into a separate client trust account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: depositing advance client fees into the firm's operating account instead of a client trust account.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 — Failure to provide competent representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to provide competent representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: not reviewing trademark applications, responses to Office Actions, and other trademark documents prepared and filed by employees; failing to comply with electronic signature rules leading to jeopardized registrations; directing or allowing employees to sign false § 2(f) declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a) — Failing to keep client reasonably informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to keep the client reasonably informed about the status of a matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: not informing a client of an Office Action or substitute specimens filed on their behalf without confirming accuracy; failing to inform clients that their registrations/applications may be invalid and failing to take remedial action or offer restitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.115(a) — Failing to hold client property separate
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to hold property of a client or third person that is in the lawyer's possession separate from the lawyer's own property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: depositing fees paid in advance by clients for trademark legal services and costs into the attorney's operating account rather than keeping them separate.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.115(c) — Failing to deposit advance fees/expenses into trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to deposit into a client trust account legal fees and expenses that have been paid in advance, to be withdrawn only as fees are earned or expenses incurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: depositing advance fees and expenses for trademark services into operating account rather than trust until earned/incurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.18 — Certifications to the USPTO (electronic signature rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certifications made to the USPTO under § 11.18 (including electronic signature and certification requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations include directing or allowing employees to sign or forge the practitioner's electronic signature on trademark applications/documents or § 2(f) declarations when the actual signatory is not identified or lacks requisite knowledge; failing to personally sign as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.303(a)(1) — Knowingly making false statement of fact to a tribunal
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowingly making a false statement of material fact to a tribunal or failing to correct a false statement previously made to the tribunal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: failing to inform the USPTO of potentially invalid applications/registrations that resulted from filing false or fraudulent specimens or digitally altered marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.303(d) — Duty to inform tribunal in ex parte proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing, in an ex parte proceeding, to inform the tribunal of all material facts known to the practitioner that will enable the tribunal to make an informed decision, even if the facts are adverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: filing § 2(f) declarations or other submissions without disclosing material adverse facts (e.g., that declarations were signed by employees lacking knowledge or that specimens were false/digitally altered).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.503(a) — Reasonable efforts by managerial authority (employee conduct compatibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to make reasonable efforts (as a partner or person of comparable managerial authority) to ensure that the firm's employees' conduct was compatible with the practitioner's professional obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: failing to adequately supervise employees or review their work, permitting false/fraudulent specimens or digitally altered marks to be filed, resulting in registrations of questionable validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.503(b) — Supervisory obligations over direct subordinates
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to make reasonable efforts to ensure that the conduct of employees over whom the practitioner has direct supervisory authority is compatible with the practitioner's professional obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples mirror 11.503(a): inadequate supervision, failure to review work, permitting false/digital specimens to be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.503(c) — Ordering/ratifying employee misconduct; remedial measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordering or ratifying employee conduct that would violate the Rules if committed by a practitioner, and/or failing to take remedial measures once the practitioner learned of the conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: failing to supervise or failing to inform clients/USPTO or take remediation/restoration after learning of employee misconduct that produced false or fraudulent specimens or declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.504(a) — Sharing legal fees with non-practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Sharing legal fees with a non-practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: paying employees non-discretionary monthly bonuses tied to proceeds from trademark legal services (constitutes an impermissible sharing of legal fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.505 — Assisting others in unauthorized practice of law before USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Assisting other persons in the unauthorized practice of law before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: directing or allowing employees to prepare/sign/file trademark applications, responses to Office Actions, and other trademark documents; allowing employees to provide legal advice/guidance or communicate with clients about trademark searches/opinions without attorney oversight; failing to review employee-prepared documents before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.701 — Making false or misleading communications about practitioner's services
rubrics_metrics.description: Making false or misleading communications about the practitioner or the practitioner's services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: advertising that applications would be prepared by an attorney when in fact they were not prepared or reviewed by an attorney prior to filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.801(b) / § 11.501(b) — Failing to cooperate with OED / respond to lawful requests for information
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to respond to lawful requests for information and failing to cooperate with the Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) in an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: telling witnesses not to talk to OED; falsely telling potential witnesses that talking to OED could affect their trademark rights; withholding names of former employees for months; not providing requested documents (invoices, employment agreements, correspondence about § 2(f) declarations, privilege log).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c) — Conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples overlap with 10.23(b)(4): not informing clients that documents were not attorney-prepared; allowing employees to sign/forge electronic signatures; filing false or fraudulent specimens; misleading potential witnesses about OED.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d) — Conduct prejudicial to administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples overlap with other provisions: directing employees to sign/forge electronic signatures or § 2(f) declarations; failing to review or supervise employee work; creating or filing false specimens or altered images; obstructing OED investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i) — Other conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in any other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all referencing acts and omissions described in other counts (e.g., falsified filings, lack of supervision, failing to cooperate with OED).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 — Affidavit for Consent Exclusion (procedural standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rule governing consent exclusion: practitioner may submit an Affidavit For Consent Exclusion under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 and the Director may approve exclusion on consent if requirements met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order notes Respondent executed a twelve-page Affidavit For Consent Exclusion pursuant to § 11.27; the Director determined the affidavit complied with § 11.27(a) and approved exclusion. The affidavit must acknowledge voluntariness and awareness of consequences, and waives certain defenses for reinstatement proceedings (see 11.60 consequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.5(b), 11.58, 11.59, 11.60 — Reinstatement and related procedural rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules concerning exclusion, compliance during exclusion, and standards/procedures for reinstatement to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent acknowledged understanding of these provisions; the affidavit concedes that upon application for reinstatement under § 11.60, the OED Director will presumptively treat the complaint allegations as true for reinstatement determination. The Order requires compliance with § 11.58 and § 11.60 for reinstatement requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptive treatment of complaint allegations for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: By consenting to exclusion, respondent acknowledges that, for purposes of any future reinstatement application, the OED Director will conclusively presume the disciplinary complaint allegations are true and that the respondent could not have successfully defended against them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a consequence of consenting to exclusion and is explicitly acknowledged in the affidavit and Order; it affects how reinstatement applications are evaluated under § 11.60.
